# `clock` commands

## `clock cancel`

Throw away a running clock started by mistake, with a reason. Records no time; the clock stays readable. An agent clocks only the person it acts for, on their instruction: its principal must be the employee's linked login (`clock link`).

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | customer-work |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/clock.cancel` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow clock cancel --employee "Casey Worker" --reason "Clocked in by mistake" --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "clock cancel", "input": {"employee": "Casey Worker"}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `employee` | `--employee` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Employee ID or name. Leave it out for your own: the employee your login is linked to (`clock link`), or, for an agent, its principal's. |

## `clock in`

Start the clock for a person: now, or at a stated time today. Optionally the customer:job, service item, class, billable and notes; they may be given at clock-out instead. One clock per person; it shows on the home page while it runs. Records nothing yet. An agent clocks only the person it acts for, on their instruction: its principal must be the employee's linked login (`clock link`).

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

## `clock link`

Say which person's login is an employee, or unlink it (no user). Then that person's own timesheet and clock need no employee named, and an agent acting for them may clock them in and out on their instruction. A person's act.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | customer-work |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/clock.link` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

## `clock out`

Stop a person's clock and record the time: one time entry per company-local day (a night shift is split at midnight), rounded per the company preference to exact hours. Needs a customer:job and service item from clock-in or here. A clock that ran past the maximum shift was probably forgotten: give the end time the person stopped. An agent clocks only the person it acts for, on their instruction: its principal must be the employee's linked login (`clock link`).

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | customer-work |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/clock.out` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow clock out --employee "Casey Worker" --reason "Casey finished" --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:


### Input

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `employee` | `--employee` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Employee ID or name. Leave it out for your own: the employee your login is linked to (`clock link`), or, for an agent, its principal's. |
| `customer` | `--customer` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Customer:job, if not given at clock-in or to change it. |
| `item` | `--item` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Service item, if not given at clock-in or to change it. |
| `class_id` | `--class-id` | string \| null | no | yes | null | — |

| `end` | `--end` | string \| null | no | yes | null | When the person stopped; now by default. Required once the clock has run past the maximum shift. A time: ISO 8601 with a zone (2026-10-20T08:00:00-07:00), or company-local YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM. |

## `clock status`

Who is clocked in: each running clock with its start, hours so far, and whether it has passed the maximum shift and must be closed with a stated end time.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | read |
| Required role | member |
| Capability | customer-work |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/clock.status` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow clock status --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "clock status", "input": {}, "company": "Company ID or name"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `employee` | `--employee` | string \| null | no | yes | null | One employee; every open clock by default. |

### Command and context options

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--json` | Print one JSON object. |
| `--data-root TEXT` | Data root; otherwise `BOOKFLOW_DATA_ROOT`, then `~/.bookflow`. |
| `--company TEXT` | Company id, `Organization/Company`, or display name. |

### HTTP

Route: `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/clock.status`

Send the input object as JSON. Authentication may instead come from a browser session cookie.

| Header | Requirement | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Authorization` | required for bearer clients | `Bearer <secret>` |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Name` | optional | Stable caller name recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Version` | optional | Caller version recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Context-Encoding` | optional | percent-utf8: encode all reason, source-ref, directive, idempotency-key, client-name and client-version header values as UTF-8 percent encoding |
| `X-Bookflow-Company` | optional | If sent, must equal the company ULID in the route |

### Output
